name: Surface Hijack Probe
summary: Not a useful module: a live app whose shared board any caller holding a different module's own permission can silently overwrite.
description: Declares one `app` extension point (`board`, gated on `own-board`). Launch it in a channel, then have anyone holding the permission of a completely different installed module POST {"module_id": "<the other module>", "command": "<its command>", "input": ""} to /messages/{thisAppsMessageId}/blocks/0/run. It succeeds and this app's shared, broadcast board is replaced by the other module's output, for every viewer, even though the caller never held `own-board` at all. `POST /messages/{id}/blocks/{n}/run` (crates/slimm-server/src/http/code_runs.rs::run) checks only that the caller can view the message and holds the *named* module's own permission (via http::module_commands::execute_command); it never checks the caller's module_id/command against the message's own app_surfaces row, which is the only place slim records which module actually launched a given app. app_surfaces itself is untouched by the overwrite - it still names this module - so the launch record and the live, rendered state can permanently disagree once this happens. Any second installed module is enough to demonstrate it; this one exists only to have a board worth defacing.
author: slim-m

permissions.name: Own the board
permissions.description: The permission that actually governs this app - never checked by the run route on a block a caller did not launch.

extension_points.name: Surface Hijack Probe
extension_points.description: Launch the probe's board, then overwrite it from an unrelated module.
